She stood in the hall. A sadness in her heart, a child on the outside, never welcomed within. She stood in the hall, looking into the world, a perpetual outsider, never welcomed within. The hall constricting, shadows grasping for light and touching her flesh. Reaching for her heart, filling it with darkness, suffocating her will. She welcomed it, her darkened heart, hardened.

The hall shifted, and she stood on a beach, an old weathered skeleton, stained by the sun, planed by the wind, matched its golden blanket. She looked upon his sunken skull, a scaffolding, surrounding a fallen monument. "It's not right you know, destroying, what you once loved. It leave's you feeling empty, your gut all twisted up. You can't tell what's right or wrong, sometimes. You see that's the problem, the knowing of a thing. Sometimes you get tired of the arguing of it. Sometimes you just do, because you're finished with thinking. You don't care what side of the coin you come down on anymore."

She gathered herself, for a moment in time, stretching all before her, the choices she had made. "It's a terrible slope, on which a girl could fall. A precedent set, a sentence passed, like the crossing of a threshold, and the entering of a room. Looking at the faces, wondering what they welcomed, and would you be discarded". So she put her foot forward, and stood on the slope. Would she drown or could she cope? Her other foot partnered it's twin, and she was gone.

She stood in the hall, steel in her heart. The shadows clawed at her, clamouring for her heart. It was hers this time, closed to the darkness. They tore at her flesh, but her heart was her own. She stepped into the world, and she found him there. "I loved you once" she said, "but you failed me. It is time we put that right, the wrongness of the past".

"I have nowhere to go" he said.

"Then I will give you a pearl, and you can make it your home". So she gathered his soul, and they left hand in hand.
